mechanism_narrative: The level of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is positively correlated with S&P 500 20-day forward returns; higher CPI levels predict positive equity returns due to inflation expectations supporting real asset valuations.
failure_condition: Rank IC of CPIAUCSL with respect to 20-day S&P 500 returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.0% signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 2.0 in 70% of instances, but 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is low (FEDFUNDS < 2.0) and the Consumer Price Index is high (CPIAUCSL > 255), the combination signals an impending monetary tightening cycle that reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (FEDFUNDS < 2.0 AND CPIAUCSL > 255) is met in 70% of instances, but 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (defined by FEDFUNDS > 2.0), the S&P 500 produces negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 2.0 in 70% of instances, but 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A labor market unemployment rate below 4.0% signals strong economic conditions that support corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 4.0 in 70% of instances, but 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth is strong (PAYEMS > 150000) and unemployment is falling (UNRATE < 4.0), the labor market signals robust economic expansion, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (PAYEMS > 150000 AND UNRATE < 4.0) is met in 70% of instances, but 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The level of industrial production (INDPRO) is negatively correlated with S&P 500 returns; higher industrial production levels indicate economic strength that reduces the relative attractiveness of equities, leading to negative returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO has a positive Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between INDPRO and 60-day returns is positive in the latest 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: In strong housing market regimes (HOUST > 1200), the S&P 500 produces positive returns over the next 5 trading days due to increased consumer spending and economic confidence.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1200 in 70% of instances, but 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
